steps.tx: **Leprosy** is a chronic granulomatous disease caused by Mycobacterium leprae, the only bacteria that invades Schwann cells and grows at 27 to 30 degree Celsius. India carries about sixty percent of new cases globally, with forty thousand to eighty thousand annual reports. Incubation lasts 3 to 12 years, and only 5% of exposed contacts develop disease. The bacillary index grades smear positivity from 0 to 6 plus on a logarithmic scale.
steps.say: Leprosy is a chronic granulomatous disease caused by mycobacterium leprae. It grows at cooler body temperatures and invades Schwann cells. India carries most new cases globally. Incubation lasts many years and only few contacts develop disease.

steps.tx: **Risk factors** include household contact with multibacillary cases, prolonged crowding, and poor nutrition. BCG vaccination gives twenty to sixty percent protection, and single dose rifampicin six hundred milligrams gives fifty seven percent protection for two years as post exposure prophylaxis. Children below fifteen years form ten percent of new cases, a marker of recent transmission. Armadillos and red squirrels are animal reservoirs, while armadillo exposure raises risk 3 fold.
steps.say: Risk factors include household contact with multibacillary cases, crowding and poor nutrition. Bc g vaccination gives partial protection. Single dose rifampicin gives about fifty seven percent protection for two years. Children form ten percent of new cases. Armadillos are animal reservoirs.

steps.tx: **Immunology** forms the Ridley Jopling spectrum from lepromatous to tuberculoid disease. Tuberculoid patients mount strong cell mediated immunity with well formed granulomas and few bacilli, while lepromatous patients show humoral dominance with foam cells and high bacillary load. The lymphocyte proliferation response is strong in ninety percent of tuberculoid cases but weak in lepromatous cases. Nerve damage follows immunity, as oedema inside rigid sheaths strangles surviving fibres within months.
steps.say: The spectrum runs from lepromatous to tuberculoid disease. Tuberculoid patients have strong cell immunity with few bacilli. Lepromatous patients have weak cell immunity with many bacilli. Nerve damage follows immunity, as swelling inside rigid sheaths strangles surviving fibres within months.

steps.tx: **Clinical features** centre on skin and nerves. Hypopigmented anaesthetic patches above 5 millimetres with satellite lesions and nerve thickening mark paucibacillary disease. Lepromatous disease shows symmetric nodules, ear lobe infiltration, loss of eyebrows, and nasal mucosal involvement causing epistaxis. The classic sign is a thickened ulnar nerve with claw hand, foot drop from common peroneal palsy, and lagophthalmos from seventh nerve failure. About ten percent develop silent nerve injury without pain.
steps.say: Skin patches with loss of sensation and thickened nerves mark early disease. Lepromatous disease shows symmetric nodules, infiltrated ear lobes and nasal involvement. The classic signs are claw hand, foot drop and inability to close the eye. About ten percent have silent nerve injury without pain.

steps.tx: **Reactional states** are the most feared events, occurring in thirty to forty percent of borderline patients. Type 1 reversal reaction gives inflamed patches, neuritis, and new nerve palsy in 6 months after therapy starts. Type 2 erythema nodosum leprosum shows fever with painful red nodules and systemic upset in ten percent of lepromatous patients. Neuritis needs steroids within two weeks to save nerve function, with recovery above eighty percent when treated promptly.
steps.say: Reactional states are the most feared events. Type one gives inflamed patches and nerve palsy after therapy starts. Type two gives fever with painful red nodules in lepromatous disease. Neuritis needs steroids within two weeks to save nerve function, with recovery above eighty percent when treated promptly.

steps.tx: **First test** is slit skin smear from earlobes, eyebrows, and elbows, with bacillary index above 4 plus indicating high infectivity. The gold standard is skin biopsy showing acid fast bacilli inside nerves with granulomas, plus polymerase chain reaction for leprae DNA. Health card sensory testing shows loss to ten gram monofilament in 30% of silent injury. Nerve conduction studies remain normal until fibre loss exceeds 50%.
steps.say: Do slit skin smears from earlobes and eyebrows. The gold standard is skin biopsy showing bacilli inside nerves. Sensory testing with monofilament detects silent nerve injury early. Nerve studies remain normal until fibre loss exceeds half.

steps.tx: **Classification** guides drugs. Paucibacillary disease has up to 5 lesions and no bacilli, while multibacillary disease has above 5 lesions or smear positivity. Multibacillary treatment is 12 months and paucibacillary 6 months under World Health Organization uniform therapy. Erythema nodosum needs thalidomide 100 to three hundred milligrams daily in men, but it is contraindicated in pregnancy. Claw hand needs splinting from diagnosis, not after deformity sets in.
steps.say: Classification guides drugs. Paucibacillary disease has few lesions, while multibacillary has many or smear positivity. Treatment runs twelve months for multibacillary and six months for paucibacillary disease. Severe red nodule reaction needs thalidomide in men. Splint claw hand from the start.

steps.tx: **First line management** is WHO multidrug therapy. Rifampicin six hundred milligrams once monthly supervised plus dapsone 100 milligrams daily and clofazimine three hundred milligrams monthly supervised with 50 milligrams daily for multibacillary disease targets 12 months. Paucibacillary disease uses the same rifampicin and dapsone without clofazimine for 6 months. Clofazimine causes brown skin pigmentation in 2 to 3 months, reversible after stopping. Monitor haemolysis with dapsone G6PD testing in 5% with deficiency.
steps.say: First line therapy is multidrug therapy. Rifampicin is supervised monthly with daily dapsone and clofazimine for twelve months. Shorter therapy serves paucibacillary disease without clofazimine. Clofazimine darkens skin in a few months and fades after stopping. Check blood counts regularly while on dapsone therapy.

steps.tx: **Nerve care** and foot care prevent permanent disability, the true aim of therapy. Prednisolone forty to sixty milligrams daily for 6 months treats neuritis with progressive palsy, tapering by ten milligrams monthly. Protective footwear, daily oil massage, and eye care with artificial tears reduce ulcers in twenty percent of patients. Physiotherapy starts within weeks of palsy, not after 6 months when contractures fix. Contact tracing must cover twenty to 30 household members per case.
steps.say: Nerve care and foot care prevent permanent disability. Prednisolone daily treats neuritis with progressive palsy, tapering slowly. Protective footwear and eye drops reduce ulcers. Physiotherapy must start within weeks of palsy, not after months. Check contacts of every new case carefully.

steps.tx: **Complications and prognosis** include lagophthalmos with corneal ulcer in fifteen percent, foot ulcers in twenty percent, and flexion contractures in twenty five percent of delayed cases. Grade 2 disability at diagnosis is above 5% in many districts, signalling late detection. With timely multidrug therapy, cure exceeds 99% and infectivity falls within days of the first rifampicin dose. Relapse is below 1% after 12 months of therapy. Deformity, however, is irreversible once fixed contractures form.
steps.say: Complications include eye exposure, foot ulcers and joint contractures in delayed cases. Disability at diagnosis reflects late detection. With timely therapy cure is above ninety nine percent. Infectivity falls within days of the first dose. But fixed deformity is irreversible once it sets in.

steps.tx: **High-yield for the exam** pairs spectrum, smears, drugs, and reactions in one frame. Bajrok classification uses lesion count of 5, nerve thickening is cardinal, and clofazimine pigmentation is a vignette clue. Single dose rifampicin six hundred milligrams is the prophylaxis dose asked yearly. Lucio phenomenon with ulcerating nodules occurs in diffuse lepromatous disease, and foot ulcer care prevents 50% of disability.
steps.say: Keep spectrum, smears, drugs and reactions in one frame. Lesion count of five separates paucibacillary from multibacillary disease. Clofazimine pigmentation is a classic clue. Single dose rifampicin is the prophylaxis dose asked yearly. Ulcerating nodules mean lucio phenomenon here today.

rows: Rifampicin six hundred milligrams single dose
